texts.preamble: Ashu Khandelwal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 29 April, 2021 Author: Vishal Mishra
texts.facts: This is the second bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Cr.P.C. for grant of bail. The applicant has been arrested on 9.3.2021 in connection with POR No. 4959/17 Forest Department, District Gwalior registered in relation to the offence punishable under Sections 2, 9, 39, 43, 44, 49B, 50, 51 of the Wild Life (Protection) Act, 1972. First application was dismissed as withdrawn vide order dated 5.4.2021 passed in M.Cr.C. No.16112/2021 with liberty to renew his prayer for bail after filing of charge sheet. It is submitted that the applicant has been falsely implicated in the case. He has not committed any offence in any manner. As per the prosecution story, on 24.12.2020 the forest department upon receiving an information from an informant has conducted a raid on a shop which is registered in the name of Bhura Pansari. Further as per the prosecution story, the aforesaid shop is registered in the name of Chandra Prakash Khandelwal in a sole proprietorship registered under the FSSAI. Charge sheet has been filed on 26.04.2021.
texts.arguments: The applicant is a first offender and he is ready to abide by all terms and conditions that may be imposed by this Court. There is no criminal history of the applicant. On these grounds, he prays for grant of bail. Per contra, counsel for the State has opposed the application and THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Ashu Khandelwal vs. State of M.P.) prays for its rejection. 3. The applicant will not indulge himself in extending inducement, THE HIGH COURT OF MADHYA PRADESH (Ashu Khandelwal vs. State of M.P.) threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or to the Police Officer, as the case may be; 4. The applicant shall not commit an offence similar to the offence of which he is accused. 5. The applicant will not seek unnecessary adjournments during the trial; and 6.
